dedupe_keys.name: global wheat maize and rice trade networks resilience and cascading failure 2015 to 2024

description: This case study builds directed, weighted trade networks for wheat, maize and rice from 2015 to 2024 and tests how vulnerable and resilient they are using a three-dimensional structural resilience framework and underload cascading failure models. The authors, researchers at Shaanxi University of Science and Technology, published it in an open-access journal article. The simulations remove key exporting countries by targeted attack, and a multilayer version lets importers substitute one crop for another. Coverage is global at country level with annual trade flows. The article is free to read under a Creative Commons Attribution licence. Caveats: the networks capture recorded bilateral trade only, and substitution willingness is a model parameter, not observed behaviour. The study found that all three networks are scale-free and disassortative; the wheat network recovered after the Russia-Ukraine conflict, the maize network became more imbalanced and the rice network depends heavily on a few exporters. Targeted attacks on key exporters can collapse large parts of a network. Crop substitution strengthens each network on its own, but under simultaneous attacks it spreads failures across crops, and even a small willingness to substitute can weaken resilience. Simulation uses: a cascading failure and network flow template for global food supply shocks. Related records: UN Comtrade (data-un-comtrade) and CEPII BACI (data-cepii-baci) supply bilateral trade flows of this kind, and FAOSTAT (data-faostat) covers production and trade of staple crops.
